jane_acme: Hey team — embedding calls from our web client started failing this morning after we rolled a small frontend change. We get a 400 and an error "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024". Also noticed a short billing spike (one extra request per user?). Repro below, happy to share logs.

jane_acme: Minimal request we send (from browser):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-large",
  "input": [["Sign up flow copy for onboarding"]]
}
```
We used our internal wrapper around fetch: `api.post('/v1/embeddings', payload)`. The SDK isn't involved — this is a raw client call. Response: `400 Bad Request {"error":"Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024"}`

elaine_support: Thanks @jane_acme — sorry for the disruption. Quick questions: (1) can you paste the exact request body (including Content-Type) from the failing network call? (2) do you ever pre-compute embeddings on-client (i.e. sending vectors) or always send raw text? (3) the billing spike — is it correlated to retry logic in the frontend?

jane_acme: Paste from network tab (headers stripped):
```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-3-large",
  "input": [["Sign up flow copy for onboarding"]]
}
```
We always send raw text. No explicit retries in client, but we use an axios interceptor that will automatically retry once on network failures.

mike_infra: Quick hypothesis: the extra nesting around `input` (i.e., `[[...]]`) looks like a classic double-wrap: your front-end mapping might wrap a single example as an array, and then some middleware (or a batch helper) wraps the whole payload again. The platform expects `input` to be either a string (single example) or an array of strings `["a","b"]`. If you pass an array of arrays it can be interpreted as pre-computed vectors (or trigger internal deserialization leading to wrong dimension inference). That would explain 1024 vs 1536: we have multiple model variants (small/large) and the server tried to interpret the inner array as a 1024-d vector.

mike_infra: Can you try sending `{"input": "Sign up flow copy for onboarding"}` or `{"input": ["Sign up flow copy for onboarding"]}` from curl and see if it succeeds? Also please paste the axios wrapper code — the retry/transform could be touching the body.

jane_acme: Tried curl with a flat string, worked fine:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":"Sign up flow copy for onboarding"}'
# 200 OK, returns embedding vector length 1536
```
So curl succeeds. I'll paste our helper: `wrapForBatch(items){ return items.map(i => [i]) }` — oh. That was the bug. We added that to conform to an internal batch API earlier and forgot it wraps single strings as single-element arrays.

elaine_support: Great find — that matches the double-wrap. Two actionables: (A) short term: change the helper so it returns `items` (flat array of strings) not arrays-of-arrays; (B) if you need client-side batching, use the server-side batching helpers or our recommended client SDK which handles input shapes. We'll also mark the error message to be clearer. For customers hitting this we can return `400` with `invalid_input_shape: expected string or array of strings` instead of dimension mismatch.

matt_eng: FYI, follow-up: we should consider a guard in the embeddings endpoint that detects nested arrays of strings and returns a more actionable error (or auto-flattens if safe). For now, support note: nested arrays are ambiguous (could be vectors). I'll open an internal ticket to add a validation rule and docs snippet.

embed-bot: Support ticket #S-2026 created for customer jane_acme referencing thread 1805000001. Assigned to eng: matt_eng, infra: mike_infra.

jane_acme: Patch deployed client-side (removed the accidental wrap). Verified end-to-end — embedding calls now return 200 and expected vector length, billing went back to baseline. Thanks for the quick help :tada:

elaine_support: Glad that fixed it. I'll close the support ticket after a 24h health check. Suggested doc update: examples for `input` shapes in the Embeddings API page (single string, array of strings) and a small note about not sending nested arrays unless you're sending precomputed vectors.

matt_eng: Adding docs PR to backlog and a lightweight validation in the runtime.

jane_acme: Thanks everyone!
